tasks.short: Check applications against each vacancy’s requirements and prepare candidates for recruiter review.

today.trigger: An application arrives in Recruitee or a manager submits a vacancy request.
steps: Confirm duties, site, shift pattern, pay range and essential requirements with the manager.
Read the application and CV in Recruitee.
Compare stated experience, qualifications and availability with the agreed requirements.
Ask the candidate about missing information and record the findings.
Decide which applications need an interview or further review.
systems: SharePoint job profiles and CAO guidance
drudgery: Repeatedly reading similar CVs.
Copying application details into review notes.
Chasing missing shift availability or certificate information.
today.time_sinks: Unclear vacancy requirements and incomplete applications create repeated reading and follow-up.

lenses.faster: Extract stated qualifications, experience and availability into an evidence table linked to the application. The recruiter checks exceptions instead of rebuilding the comparison for every candidate.
lenses.autonomous: A new application triggers extraction and checks against an approved vacancy checklist. Missing or ambiguous information goes into a review queue; progression and rejection require a recruiter decision.
lenses.ambitious: Give every applicant a consistent review, including during seasonal peaks. Track which requirements actually predict productivity and retention after 90 days.
lenses.joy: Remove copying and repeated CV reading. Keep the conversations that uncover transferable experience and help candidates understand the job.
lenses.options: Show the candidate’s evidence against the essential requirements and against a version allowing training after hire. Separate missing evidence from a confirmed mismatch.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter maintains vacancy checklists and audits extraction errors, overrides and outcomes. Screening becomes a process to improve rather than a pile of applications to clear.
reach: Help HR Business Partners clarify essential job requirements.
Help Learning and Development identify qualifications that can be obtained after hiring.

tasks.human_edge: Recognising transferable skills, resolving ambiguous evidence and making a fair progression decision remain with the recruiter.
tasks.pattern_why: An llm_step extracts application facts inside a controlled workflow; the recruiter approves consequential decisions. The earlier automate classification fits preparation better than unrestricted applicant selection.

in_practice.trigger: A new or materially updated application enters a configured Recruitee stage.
steps: Load the approved vacancy checklist and application through an authorised integration.
Extract only relevant stated facts, retaining source references and marking uncertainty.
Apply explicit requirement checks without inventing qualifications or assigning an overall suitability score.
Prepare a comparison and draft questions for missing information.
Present the evidence to the recruiter and record the approved next step.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter checks the evidence and approves every progression or rejection; no applicant is excluded automatically.
systems: Recruitee through a verified API or controlled export
Integration service with an audit log
data_needed: Current vacancy requirements and their business justification
Applications and CVs with source locations
Agreed rules for handling missing information
Retention, access and model-processing arrangements
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate notes and a restricted audit log containing checklist version, evidence references, reviewer and decision.

evidence.claim: Models can extract stated application facts into structured fields, but accuracy needs testing on Noordhaven’s applications.
The proposed workflow could reduce recruiter handling time by 50%; the 1.7-times end-to-end speedup is an untested estimate.

risks: Extraction errors or proxy discrimination could wrongly disadvantage applicants.
AI used to analyse or filter applications can fall within EU AI Act high-risk employment uses; assess classification and applicable obligations before deployment.
Rubber-stamp review would undermine meaningful human oversight and could create AVG/GDPR automated-decision concerns.
CVs contain personal data that needs restricted access, limited retention and an approved processing arrangement.
research_questions: How accurately does extraction work on a representative sample of Dutch, multilingual and nonstandard applications?
Which vacancy requirements are essential at entry, and which can be met through training?
Can Recruitee support the required trigger, evidence notes and approval controls through the available integration?
Does the pilot reduce handling time without worsening missed candidates, complaints or 90-day hiring outcomes?

tasks.short: Explain the job, shifts, pay and working conditions to applicants.

today.trigger: A candidate asks about a vacancy or reaches a recruiter conversation or offer stage.
steps: Find the current vacancy details and applicable employment terms.
Check site, shift pattern, pay scale, allowances and benefits.
Explain duties, working conditions and progression opportunities.
Answer questions or ask Payroll, Compensation and Benefits or the manager for clarification.
Record what was explained and send any follow-up information.
systems: AFAS Profit for authorised employment-term references
drudgery: Repeating basic explanations about shifts and sites.
Finding the right version of pay and allowance guidance.
Writing similar follow-up emails.
today.time_sinks: Questions cross vacancy details, CAO rules and local working practices, so answers often require several lookups.

lenses.faster: Build vacancy-specific answers from approved job and employment-term information. Routine explanations and follow-up emails no longer require separate lookups and drafting.
lenses.autonomous: An applicant question receives an approved factual answer when the vacancy and relevant policy version are clear. Individual pay commitments, disputed terms and unclear questions go to the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Give applicants a realistic picture of each site and shift before interview. Explain terms in accessible language so fewer people accept an offer based on mistaken expectations.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated policy searches and basic FAQ replies. Keep the discussions about whether the work fits a person’s circumstances.
lenses.options: Offer short, detailed and translated explanations using the same approved facts. Show shift examples and approved pay illustrations without making individual promises.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the candidate information service and checks which unanswered questions or misunderstandings lead to declined offers and early exits.
reach: Maintain candidate-facing benefits explanations with Compensation and Benefits.
Prepare pre-start information packs with HR Administrators.

tasks.human_edge: Building trust and discussing personal concerns require a recruiter who can listen, clarify and avoid promises the company cannot keep.
tasks.pattern_why: Language generation can explain approved facts inside a deterministic routing process. Employment terms and pay calculations come from controlled sources and rules.

in_practice.trigger: A candidate submits a question through a configured recruitment channel.
steps: Identify the vacancy, site and question topic using only necessary candidate information.
Retrieve the current approved job facts and applicable CAO explanations.
Generate an answer with source references and use rule-based calculations for approved pay illustrations.
Send routine answers within approved boundaries and route unsupported or individual matters to the recruiter.
Record the answer and flag recurring information gaps for content review.
in_practice.human_gate: Compensation and Benefits approves term explanations before use; the recruiter handles individual commitments, exceptions and sensitive conversations.
systems: Outlook or a configured candidate question channel
data_needed: Approved vacancy facts by site and shift
Versioned CAO pay scales, allowances and benefits explanations
Escalation rules and named content owners
Approved translations and pay illustration rules
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee communication history and a restricted answer log recording source versions and escalations.

evidence.claim: A retrieval-based assistant can draft answers from approved documents, with rule-based calculations and escalation controls.
The estimated 65% handling-time saving and two-times end-to-end speedup depend on the share of routine questions.

risks: Using the wrong CAO, site arrangement or policy version could misstate pay and working conditions.
Generated language may turn an illustration into an apparent employment promise.
Incorrect translations could obscure important shift or safety information.
Candidate questions may contain sensitive personal information that should be routed privately and retained only when necessary.
research_questions: What proportion of questions can be answered from approved, current material without individual interpretation?
Who owns updates to CAO terms, site details and candidate-facing explanations?
Can applicants reliably reach a person when an answer is unclear or their circumstances are individual?
Does better pre-interview information improve offer acceptance and reduce expectation-related exits within 90 days?

tasks.short: Choose applicants to put forward and explain hiring recommendations to managers.

today.trigger: An application review, interview or work sample produces enough evidence for a hiring recommendation.
steps: Review application evidence, interview feedback and any assessment results.
Clarify missing or conflicting evidence with the candidate or interviewers.
Compare evidence with the agreed job criteria.
Write a recommendation and discuss it with the hiring manager.
Record the decision and agreed next step in Recruitee.
systems: SharePoint interview guides and selection criteria
drudgery: Combining feedback from several interviewers.
Chasing incomplete scorecards.
Rewriting evidence into manager briefing notes.
today.time_sinks: Late feedback, conflicting opinions and vague criteria delay decisions and create repeated discussions.

lenses.faster: Prepare a source-linked briefing that combines application evidence and interviewer feedback. The recruiter spends more time resolving the decision and less time assembling the pack.
lenses.autonomous: Completed interview feedback triggers briefing preparation and missing-evidence reminders. The system does not choose the shortlist or recommend a winner.
lenses.ambitious: Make every hiring recommendation traceable to job-relevant evidence. Review which decisions lead to productive hires who stay beyond 90 days.
lenses.joy: Remove feedback chasing and repeated briefing drafts. Keep the judgement, candidate advocacy and manager conversations.
lenses.options: Show evidence gaps, disagreements and the consequences of different entry requirements. The recruiter can consider further assessment, training or another candidate without receiving a machine-generated ranking.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter improves the quality of hiring decisions across managers by maintaining interview standards and reviewing decision patterns.
reach: Coach hiring managers on structured interviews with HR Business Partners.
Support onboarding handovers by summarising agreed training needs.

tasks.human_edge: The recruiter and manager weigh incomplete evidence, challenge unfair assumptions and take responsibility for the hiring recommendation.
tasks.pattern_why: AI helps organise and summarise evidence while the recruiter leads comparison, judgement and communication.

in_practice.trigger: The required interview feedback is submitted or a hiring decision meeting is scheduled.
steps: Collect authorised candidate evidence and the approved job criteria.
Summarise each criterion with source references, separating facts from interviewer opinions.
Flag missing evidence and conflicting feedback without producing a candidate rank.
Let the recruiter edit the briefing and make the recommendation.
Record the manager’s decision, rationale and any agreed onboarding needs.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter owns the recommendation and the hiring manager approves the decision after reviewing the evidence.
data_needed: Approved selection criteria
Applications, interview feedback and relevant assessment evidence
Decision authority and escalation rules
A structured decision-rationale template
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee decision notes containing the final rationale, evidence references and responsible decision-makers.

evidence.claim: Models can summarise interview notes and expose missing or conflicting evidence for human review.
The estimated 30% handling-time saving and 1.3-times speedup assume assembly work falls while decision conversations remain.

risks: A polished summary can hide uncertainty or amplify biased interviewer comments.
Managers may treat the briefing as a decision rather than examine its evidence.
AI assistance that materially influences selection may fall within EU AI Act high-risk employment uses despite having a human reviewer.
Interview notes may contain irrelevant or sensitive personal data that should not enter the briefing.
research_questions: How much current time goes into assembling evidence versus making and discussing the decision?
Do summaries preserve source meaning and uncertainty across different interviewers?
Do managers challenge the evidence and document their own reasoning when using the briefing?
Does structured decision evidence improve manager satisfaction and 90-day outcomes without increasing unfair exclusions?

tasks.short: Keep applicants informed about progress, delays and decisions.

today.trigger: An application changes stage, a decision is approved or a candidate asks for an update.
steps: Check the current stage, decision and expected next step.
Confirm that the candidate can be told the outcome.
Write or adapt a message and send it by email or phone.
Record the contact in Recruitee.
Follow up if the process stalls or the candidate replies.
drudgery: Sending repeated acknowledgement and progress messages.
Checking which candidates have not received an update.
Copying messages between Outlook and the applicant record.
today.time_sinks: Unrecorded manager decisions and stalled stages force the recruiter to chase information before contacting candidates.

lenses.faster: Send approved status templates directly from recorded process events. Manual drafting, inbox checks and contact logging disappear for routine updates.
lenses.autonomous: Stage changes and elapsed-time rules trigger acknowledgements, progress updates and delay notices. Rejection messages require an already approved decision, and sensitive cases go to the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Set a clear maximum silence period for every applicant, including seasonal peaks. Measure whether updates reduce withdrawals and repeated status enquiries.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive emails and diary reminders. Keep personal calls where the relationship or explanation matters.
lenses.options: Use approved variants by stage, language and contact preference. Offer a factual next-step explanation without inventing a completion date.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns candidate communication standards and monitors silence, delivery failures and stalled decisions.
reach: Help hiring managers manage interview-feedback deadlines.
Coordinate the accepted-candidate handover to HR Administrators.

tasks.human_edge: Personal explanations, difficult rejections and relationship repair need a recruiter who understands the candidate and the decision.
tasks.pattern_why: Recorded events, approved templates and explicit send rules cover most status communication without a model at runtime.

in_practice.trigger: An approved stage transition occurs or a candidate reaches the configured update deadline.
steps: Check the candidate’s current stage, decision approval and most recent contact.
Select the approved template using stage, vacancy and recorded language preference.
Validate recipient, permitted status and required fields, and block duplicate messages.
Send routine updates; route sensitive outcomes, replies and delivery failures to the recruiter.
Record delivery and create a follow-up task where the process remains stalled.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter approves message rules and templates; consequential decisions must be authorised before any outcome message is sent.
systems: Integration service for unsupported timing or logging rules
data_needed: Reliable stage and decision-approval fields
Approved communication templates
Update deadlines and escalation owners
Language and contact preferences
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee communication history and a workflow log recording event, template version, delivery and exceptions.

evidence.claim: Recruitee provides automated actions, including email actions linked to recruitment workflow events.
The estimated 75% handling-time saving and three-times speedup depend on reliable stage updates and the proportion of personal calls.

risks: An incorrect stage transition could send an inappropriate outcome message.
Duplicate or contradictory messages can result from overlapping Outlook and Recruitee workflows.
Delay templates could imply progress that has not occurred.
Automated messages may feel impersonal when a candidate has invested substantial time in interviews.
research_questions: Which necessary event, timing and approval checks can the current Recruitee subscription support?
How often are stages accurate and updated promptly by recruiters and managers?
What share of contacts need a personal call rather than a standard message?
Does the pilot reduce candidate silence and status enquiries without increasing incorrect or duplicate messages?

tasks.short: Find candidates for warehouse, transport and office vacancies across our three sites.

today.trigger: A vacancy opens, a pipeline is weak or seasonal demand requires more candidates.
steps: Clarify the role, site, shifts and realistic search requirements.
Search permitted candidate records, recruiting channels and referral sources.
Review potential candidates and identify relevant evidence.
Write outreach or coordinate referrals, campaigns, fairs and agency searches.
Record responses and assess which sources produce suitable applicants.
drudgery: Rewriting search queries and outreach messages.
Checking duplicate candidate records.
Manually combining source and response reports.
today.time_sinks: Broad searches produce irrelevant results, while fragmented records make it difficult to learn which sources deliver retained hires.

lenses.faster: Draft search queries, organise permitted results and prepare outreach from an approved vacancy brief. The recruiter spends less time formatting and more time evaluating sources and candidates.
lenses.autonomous: An approved vacancy triggers a sourcing brief and permitted searches where integrations allow them. The recruiter reviews candidate evidence and approves outreach before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain useful pipelines by site, shift and job family before peaks arrive. Compare sources by productive hires retained at 90 days, rather than application volume alone.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated search setup, deduplication and message drafting. Keep networking, referral conversations and candidate relationships.
lenses.options: Compare agency, referral, local-event and advertising approaches with different costs and expected lead times. Generate several search formulations without using protected characteristics or inferred personal traits.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter designs a sourcing portfolio and improves it using cost and downstream hiring outcomes.
reach: Support employer-brand content with hiring managers.
Help People Analytics connect recruitment sources to 90-day outcomes.
Coordinate approved seasonal sourcing briefs with staffing agencies.

tasks.human_edge: Judging local labour-market realities, building networks and choosing respectful outreach remain personal work.
tasks.pattern_why: AI accelerates search preparation, evidence organisation and drafting, while the recruiter controls sources, candidate review and contact.

in_practice.trigger: A vacancy is approved or a monitored pipeline falls below an agreed level.
steps: Load the approved vacancy brief, source budget and allowed sourcing channels.
Draft search queries and channel-specific campaign options.
Run only authorised searches and check existing records for duplicates and contact restrictions.
Prepare source-linked candidate notes and outreach drafts for recruiter review.
Record approved contacts and measure responses, hires and 90-day outcomes.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter approves sourcing channels, candidate inclusion and each outreach batch; campaign spending follows existing budget authority.
systems: Staffing agency portals where access is authorised
data_needed: Approved vacancy briefs and sourcing budgets
Permitted candidate records and contact restrictions
Source identifiers, campaign costs and response data
Approved linkage to hire and 90-day outcome data
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee source and contact records, with campaign costs and aggregate outcomes in the recruitment reporting dataset.

evidence.claim: Models can draft search queries and outreach variants and organise supplied candidate evidence.
The estimated 40% handling-time saving and 1.5-times speedup assume authorised access to usable candidate sources.

risks: Search criteria can reproduce bias or exclude candidates through unnecessary requirements.
Publicly visible information does not remove AVG/GDPR obligations for collecting and contacting prospects.
Scraping or automated platform access may breach platform terms or exceed authorised access.
An old talent pool can contain expired permissions, objections or records due for deletion.
research_questions: Which sources permit the proposed searches and integrations, and which must remain manual?
What lawful basis, privacy notice, retention period and objection handling apply to each sourcing channel?
Can source and campaign costs be linked reliably to productive hires retained after 90 days?
Do assisted searches improve relevant response rates across the three sites without narrowing access unfairly?

tasks.short: Check that our hiring criteria and assessments are relevant, fair and supported by evidence.

today.trigger: A selection method changes, a complaint occurs or a periodic hiring-quality review is due.
steps: Collect job criteria, interview guides and assessment rules.
Check their job relevance and review candidate or manager concerns.
Compare selection patterns with available hiring outcomes.
Consult HR, privacy, legal or assessment specialists on unresolved issues.
Recommend revisions and document the approved criteria.
drudgery: Comparing versions of interview guides.
Rebuilding selection-rate tables.
Assembling the same review evidence for different vacancies.
today.time_sinks: Small samples, inconsistent criteria and weak links between selection evidence and later performance limit meaningful conclusions.

lenses.faster: Compile criterion versions, outcome tables and documented exceptions into a review pack. The recruiter can concentrate on whether the criteria are defensible and useful.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled review or changed assessment triggers version checks and predefined statistical reports. Claims of validity, fairness and legal compliance require qualified human interpretation.
lenses.ambitious: Review every recurring job family against later productivity and retention. Remove entry requirements that add barriers without evidence of job relevance.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet rebuilding and document comparison. Keep the work of improving hiring standards with managers and specialists.
lenses.options: Compare the current criteria with training-first alternatives and different assessment thresholds. Show sample size and uncertainty alongside each comparison.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter becomes the owner of selection quality, with explicit standards, review dates and evidence requirements.
reach: Develop recruitment-quality reporting with People Analytics.
Support HR Business Partners in revising job profiles.
Prepare selection-process evidence for HR Director, privacy and OR discussions.

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting fairness, job relevance and statistical uncertainty requires judgement and, for specialist assessments, qualified expertise.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic calculations and AI-assisted document review prepare evidence; accountable people interpret it and approve changes.

in_practice.trigger: A quarterly review is due or a selection criterion or tool is proposed for change.
steps: Collect versioned criteria, selection records and approved outcome measures.
Run predefined data-quality and statistical checks, reporting missingness, sample sizes and uncertainty.
Draft a review pack linking each criterion to its stated job requirement and supporting evidence.
Review findings with People Analytics and relevant privacy, legal or assessment specialists.
Complete any required OR process, approve revisions and publish the new controlled version.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter and HR Director approve changes within their authority; specialists assess validity and legal questions, and OR consent or consultation is obtained where applicable.
data_needed: Criteria and assessment versions
Selection stages, decisions and documented exceptions
Agreed productivity and 90-day retention measures
A lawful and proportionate plan for any equality monitoring data
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint selection-governance register, with controlled analysis outputs in the HR reporting environment.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports repeatable analysis using related datasets and reusable measures.
Determining assessment validity or fairness needs appropriate data, study design and qualified interpretation.
The estimated 35% handling-time saving and 1.4-times speedup are untested and depend on data quality.

risks: Small samples or confounding factors can produce misleading conclusions about criteria.
Retention alone can reinforce past hiring patterns and does not establish job performance or fairness.
Equality analysis may involve sensitive data that cannot simply be inferred or collected for convenience.
Changing recruitment policy or introducing selection AI may require OR involvement and assessment of EU AI Act obligations.
research_questions: Are selection records and criterion versions complete enough to reproduce past decisions?
Is productivity defined consistently, and are sample sizes sufficient for the proposed comparisons?
Which analyses require an assessment specialist, and what equality data can lawfully be used?
Which proposed changes require OR consent or consultation and further AI Act or privacy assessment?

tasks.short: Plan recruiting activity around site demand, seasonal peaks and expected staffing gaps.

today.trigger: Managers request hiring, seasonal plans change or staffing forecasts show a gap.
steps: Collect demand, vacancies, expected turnover and flex-worker requirements by site.
Review recruitment capacity, pipeline conversion and time to hire.
Choose channels, timing and priorities with managers and HR Business Partners.
Agree budgets, agency support and onboarding constraints.
Track results and adjust the plan.
drudgery: Combining vacancy, headcount and agency reports.
Rebuilding hiring forecasts in spreadsheets.
Preparing repeated planning updates.
today.time_sinks: Demand changes faster than reporting, and recruitment plans often lack a shared view of onboarding and training capacity.

lenses.faster: Combine staffing demand and pipeline data into a repeatable planning view. Calculate required applications and starts using explicit conversion and retention assumptions.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly refresh produces gap alerts and scenario drafts; a major demand change triggers an additional review. Hiring priorities, spending and agency commitments stay with accountable people.
lenses.ambitious: Plan backwards from productive hires still employed at day 90, rather than vacancy counts. Include week-one onboarding and mandatory training capacity before increasing recruitment volume.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet consolidation and recurring slide preparation. Keep the discussions that balance operations, candidate supply and quality of hire.
lenses.options: Compare direct hiring, referrals, agency support and phased starts under different demand and retention assumptions. Show cost, lead time and onboarding pressure for each scenario.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter manages the flow from staffing demand to retained productive hires and helps managers address constraints beyond candidate supply.
reach: Support HR Business Partners with workforce-demand scenarios.
Prepare recruitment and flex-cost assumptions for FP&A.
Coordinate start-date capacity with HR Administrators and Learning and Development.

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating credible demand, prioritising scarce capacity and choosing commitments under uncertainty require recruiter and operational judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules and analytical models calculate scenarios; AI drafts explanations while the recruiter leads planning and coordination.

in_practice.trigger: The weekly planning cycle runs or an approved staffing-demand change is recorded.
steps: Load approved demand, headcount, vacancies, pipeline, agency and onboarding-capacity data.
Check data timestamps and separate direct employees from agency workers.
Calculate staffing gaps and application-to-retained-hire scenarios using explicit assumptions.
Draft a plan showing recruitment capacity, costs, training constraints and unresolved decisions.
Review with managers, HR Business Partners and relevant budget owners, then track approved actions.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers validate demand; the recruiter approves recruitment actions, and authorised owners approve budgets and agency commitments.
data_needed: Staffing demand by site, role, shift and week
Vacancies, pipeline conversion, offer acceptance and time to hire
Aggregate turnover and availability assumptions
Agency lead times and costs
Onboarding and mandatory training capacity
Agreed productivity and 90-day retention definitions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint recruitment-plan register and Power BI scenario history with assumptions, approvals and actions.

evidence.claim: Power BI and Excel can combine planning inputs and calculate repeatable scenarios; company integrations still need implementation.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Excel

evidence.claim: The estimated 35% handling-time saving and 1.4-times speedup depend on consistent demand inputs and fewer manual reconciliations.

risks: Nightly AFAS extracts can lag operational changes and create false precision.
Employee and agency-worker counts can be double-counted or measured on different bases.
An optimistic plan can overwhelm onboarding, certificate training or manager capacity.

Individual absence or health information should not become recruiter planning data; use approved aggregate availability, with absence management and Wet verbetering poortwachter work remaining with the responsible HR team.
research_questions: Who supplies and approves weekly demand by site and shift, and how accurate is it?
Can candidate, employee and agency data be reconciled without double-counting?
What limits successful starts: candidate supply, offer acceptance, onboarding, training or early retention?
Do scenario forecasts improve retained productive hires and cost predictability compared with current planning?

tasks.short: Arrange job-relevant applicant tests and review what the results tell us.

today.trigger: A hiring process needs an assessment or an existing test is scheduled for review.
steps: Define the job skill or requirement the assessment should measure.
Select or develop the assessment with managers and appropriate specialists.
Arrange instructions, scheduling and reasonable adjustments.
Administer the assessment and record results.
Review results and candidate experience, then revise the method where needed.
systems: Studytube for relevant training and certificate requirements
drudgery: Scheduling sessions and sending repeated instructions.
Copying scores into candidate records.
Producing result summaries and checking assessment versions.
today.time_sinks: Designing valid assessments, arranging safe practical sessions and interpreting ambiguous results require coordination and specialist input.

lenses.faster: Draft job-relevant work samples and instructions, automate scheduling and calculate approved objective scores. The recruiter and specialists retain design approval and interpretation.
lenses.autonomous: An approved assessment stage triggers invitations, reminders and result collection. Only fixed scoring rules run automatically; ambiguous, practical and subjective results need review.
lenses.ambitious: Use short, accessible work samples that reflect actual warehouse, transport and office tasks. Evaluate whether they add useful evidence beyond interviews without imposing unnecessary candidate effort.
lenses.joy: Remove scheduling, score copying and repeated instructions. Keep observing relevant skills and discussing how people approach real work.
lenses.options: Prepare several assessment formats measuring the same skill, with appropriate adjustments. Compare candidate burden, safety, scoring reliability and evidence of usefulness.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter manages an approved assessment catalogue with owners, versions, accessibility rules and review dates.
reach: Co-design practical work samples with Learning and Development and site trainers.
Coordinate assessment-quality analysis with People Analytics.
Coach managers on consistent observation and scoring.

tasks.human_edge: Qualified people establish validity, make adjustments, supervise practical safety and interpret results in context.
tasks.pattern_why: AI supports design drafts and summaries; deterministic software handles administration and objective scoring. Specialist judgement remains central to assessment use.

in_practice.trigger: A candidate reaches an approved assessment stage or an assessment review date arrives.
steps: Select the approved assessment version and confirm adjustment and supervision needs.
Send instructions and schedule the session using controlled templates.
Collect results through the approved assessment process; supervise practical work where required.
Apply fixed scoring rules and draft an evidence summary without a hiring verdict.
Have the recruiter and assessor review results and record the approved interpretation.
in_practice.human_gate: Qualified owners approve assessment design, thresholds and adjustments; assessors supervise practical tests, and people approve interpretation and hiring decisions.
systems: Approved assessment tool if one is selected
Excel or a controlled scoring service
Studytube for training requirements, without assuming it is an applicant-testing platform
data_needed: Job-skill definitions and assessment purpose
Approved instructions, rubrics and evidence supporting use
Candidate adjustment requests with restricted access
Assessment versions, results and assessor observations
Practical safety and supervision requirements
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted assessment records linked to Recruitee, with versions and approval history in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, reminders and fixed scoring can be automated, while models can draft work samples and instructions for expert review.
AI-generated assessment items do not establish psychometric validity, safety or fairness.
The estimated 30% handling-time saving and 1.3-times speedup depend on how much work is administration rather than supervised assessment.

risks: Generated tests can appear credible while failing to measure the intended job skill.
Language, disability or digital-access barriers can distort scores without suitable adjustments.
Practical warehouse or driving tests need appropriate safety controls; a work sample does not replace a required certificate.

AI scoring or evaluation may trigger EU AI Act high-risk employment obligations; workplace emotion inference is prohibited except for specified medical or safety reasons and has no place in this workflow.
Medical or psychological assessments require specialist and legal review, including Dutch restrictions on pre-employment medical examinations.
research_questions: Which current assessments have evidence of job relevance, reliable scoring and usefulness for later performance?
What share of assessment time is administration versus specialist design, supervision and interpretation?
Can candidates receive suitable adjustments without changing the skill being measured?
Does a pilot work sample improve hiring evidence and candidate experience without creating safety, fairness or privacy problems?

role.altitude: The recruiter becomes the owner of hiring flow and decision quality across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, improving the system from approved vacancy to a productive hire retained after 90 days.
reach: Support HR Business Partners with job requirements and workforce-demand scenarios.
Coordinate pre-start and week-one handovers with HR Administrators.
Co-design job-relevant work samples and training-first hiring routes with Learning and Development.
Develop source-to-90-day outcome reporting with People Analytics.
Prepare recruitment and agency-cost scenarios with FP&A.
Help managers improve interview evidence and timely hiring decisions.
role.ceiling_note: The current workflows are inferred from the supplied systems and task statements, not observed. Estimated savings across these eight tasks total about 1,248 hours annually for both recruiters, roughly 39% of their implied combined 3,200-hour task-time baseline and about EUR 81,000 of capacity at EUR 65/hour; this is redeployable capacity, not a cash saving or an approved headcount reduction. Task handling savings and end-to-end speedups are separate, untested estimates, and integration work, quality checks and overlap can reduce the realised benefit. Interviews, relationships, accountable hiring decisions, specialist assessment, manager response times and onboarding capacity limit further gains.
skills_to_grow: Writing clear job requirements and structured interview rubrics.
Checking extracted evidence, uncertainty and automation errors.
Understanding AVG/GDPR, applicable EU AI Act duties and OR involvement in recruitment changes.
Using recruitment funnel, source-cost and 90-day outcome analysis.
Designing workflow triggers, approval gates, exception queues and audit records with the HRIS analyst.
Coaching managers and coordinating onboarding and training capacity.
Evaluating assessment validity with qualified specialists.
role.ambitious_version: Run a site-and-shift hiring service that plans backwards from productive hires retained at day 90. Use the released capacity to build local candidate relationships, improve realistic job information, coach hiring managers and remove onboarding bottlenecks. Give each recurring job family a reviewed selection process and compare sourcing, offers and start-date plans using shared outcome definitions.
